   396→    def verify_python(self, app: AppConfig):
   397→        """Verify that the version of Python being used to build the app in Docker is
   398→        compatible with the version being used to run Briefcase.
   399→
   400→        Will raise an exception if the Python version is fundamentally
   401→        incompatible (i.e., if Briefcase doesn't support it); any other version
   402→        discrepancy will log a warning, but continue.
   403→
   404→        Requires that the app tools have been verified.
   405→
   406→        As a side effect of verifying Python, the `python_version_tag` will be
   407→        updated to reflect the *actual* python version, not just a generic "3".
   408→
   409→        :param app: The application being built
   410→        """
   411→        output = self.tools[app].app_context.check_output(
   412→            [
   413→                f"python{app.python_version_tag}",
   414→                "-c",
   415→                (
   416→                    "import sys; "
   417→                    "print(f'{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}')"
   418→                ),
   419→            ]
   420→        )
   421→        # Update the python version tag with the *actual* python version.
   422→        app.python_version_tag = output.split("\n")[0]
   423→        target_python_version = tuple(int(v) for v in app.python_version_tag.split("."))
   424→
   425→        if target_python_version < self.briefcase_required_python_version:
   426→            briefcase_min_version = ".".join(
   427→                str(v) for v in self.briefcase_required_python_version
   428→            )
   429→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   430→                f"The system python3 version provided by {app.target_image} "
   431→                f"is {app.python_version_tag}; Briefcase requires a "
   432→                f"minimum Python3 version of {briefcase_min_version}."
   433→            )
   434→        elif target_python_version != (
   435→            self.tools.sys.version_info.major,
   436→            self.tools.sys.version_info.minor,
   437→        ):
   438→            self.logger.warning(
   439→                f"""
   440→*************************************************************************
   441→** WARNING: Python version mismatch!                                   **
   442→*************************************************************************
   443→
   444→    The system python3 provided by {app.target_image} is {app.python_version_tag}.
   445→    This is not the same as your local system ({self.python_version_tag}).
   446→
   447→    Ensure you have tested for Python version compatibility before
   448→    releasing this app.
   449→
   450→*************************************************************************
   451→"""
   452→            )

   454→    def verify_system_python(self):

   476→        requirements.
   477→
   478→        :param app: The app being built.
   479→        :returns: A triple containing (0) The list of package names that must
   480→            be installed at a bare minimum; (1) the arguments for the command
   481→            used to verify the existence of a package on a system, and (2)
   482→            the command used to install packages. All three values are `None`
   483→            if the system cannot be identified.
   484→        """
   485→        if app.target_vendor_base == DEBIAN:
   486→            base_system_packages = ["python3-dev", "build-essential"]
   487→            system_verify = ["dpkg", "-s"]
   488→            system_installer = ["apt", "install"]
   489→        elif app.target_vendor_base == RHEL:
   490→            base_system_packages = [
   491→                "python3-devel",
   492→                "gcc",
   493→                "make",
   494→                "pkgconf-pkg-config",
   495→            ]
   496→            system_verify = ["rpm", "-q"]
   497→            system_installer = ["dnf", "install"]
   498→        elif app.target_vendor_base == SUSE:
   499→            base_system_packages = [
   500→                "python3-devel",
   501→                "patterns-devel-base-devel_basis",
   502→            ]
   503→            system_verify = ["rpm", "-q", "--whatprovides"]
   504→            system_installer = ["zypper", "install"]
   505→        elif app.target_vendor_base == ARCH:
   506→            base_system_packages = [
   507→                "python3",
   508→                "base-devel",
   509→            ]
   510→            system_verify = ["pacman", "-Q"]
   511→            system_installer = ["pacman", "-Syu"]
   512→        else:
   513→            base_system_packages = None
   514→            system_verify = None
   515→            system_installer = None

   517→        return (

   523→    def verify_system_packages(self, app: AppConfig):
   524→        """Verify that the required system packages are installed.
   525→
   526→        :param app: The app being built.
   527→        """
   528→        (
   529→            base_system_packages,
   530→            system_verify,
   531→            system_installer,
   532→        ) = self._system_requirement_tools(app)
   533→
   534→        if not (system_verify and self.tools.shutil.which(system_verify[0])):
   535→            self.logger.warning(
   536→                """
   537→*************************************************************************
   538→** WARNING: Can't verify system packages                               **
   539→*************************************************************************
   540→
   541→    Briefcase doesn't know how to verify the installation of system
   542→    packages on your Linux distribution. If you have any problems
   543→    building this app, ensure that the packages listed in the app's
   544→    `system_requires` setting have been installed.
   545→
   546→*************************************************************************
   547→"""
   548→            )
   549→            return
   550→
   551→        # Run a check for each package listed in the app's system_requires,
   552→        # plus the baseline system packages that are required.
   553→        missing = []
   554→        for package in base_system_packages + getattr(app, "system_requires", []):
   555→            try:
   556→                self.tools.subprocess.check_output(system_verify + [package])
   557→            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
   558→                missing.append(package)
   559→
   560→        # If any required packages are missing, raise an error.
   561→        if missing:
   562→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   563→                f"""\
   564→Unable to build {app.app_name} due to missing system dependencies. Run:
   565→
   566→    sudo {" ".join(system_installer)} {" ".join(missing)}
   567→
   568→to install the missing dependencies, and re-run Briefcase.
   569→"""
   570→            )

   572→    def verify_app_tools(self, app: AppConfig):
   573→        """Verify App environment is prepared and available.
   574→
   575→        When Docker is used, create or update a Docker image for the App. Without
   576→        Docker, the host machine will be used as the App environment.
   577→
   578→        :param app: The application being built
   579→        """
   580→        # Verifying the App context is idempotent; but we have some
   581→        # additional logic that we only want to run the first time through.
   582→        # Check (and store) the pre-verify app tool state.
   583→        verify_python = not hasattr(self.tools[app], "app_context")
   584→
   585→        if self.use_docker:
   586→            DockerAppContext.verify(
   587→                tools=self.tools,
   588→                app=app,
   589→                image_tag=self.docker_image_tag(app),
   590→                dockerfile_path=self.bundle_path(app) / "Dockerfile",
   591→                app_base_path=self.base_path,
   592→                host_bundle_path=self.bundle_path(app),
   593→                host_data_path=self.data_path,
   594→                python_version=app.python_version_tag,

   596→
   597→            # Check the system Python on the target system to see if it is
   598→            # compatible with Briefcase.
   599→            if verify_python:
   600→                self.verify_python(app)
   601→        else:
   602→            NativeAppContext.verify(tools=self.tools, app=app)
   603→
   604→            # Check the system Python on the target system to see if it is
   605→            # compatible with Briefcase, and that the required system packages
   606→            # are installed.
   607→            if verify_python:
   608→                self.verify_system_python()
   609→                self.verify_system_packages(app)
   610→
   611→        # Establish Docker as app context before letting super set subprocess
   612→        super().verify_app_tools(app)
